text: CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-SRM-01 | TRAINING ONLY SERVICE REQUEST MANAGEMENT Purpose, service channels & document map CH-SRM-01 | Version 1.0 | Effective 01 Sep 2026 About Cedarhaven. The Town of Cedarhaven is a fictional Ontario municipality created for a technical recruitment exercise. This operational guide describes its simulated municipal 311 service-request process. It is not a real government policy, contact directory or statement of Canadian law. Core service promise. Residents can report non-emergency municipal service issues through one front door, receive a tracking number, and check progress. Submitting a request does not guarantee that the Town will approve a permit, issue a by-law penalty, or complete work by a particular date. Use this guide for • Missed curbside waste collection and damaged municipal bins. • Potholes, damaged street signs, municipal streetlights and blocked catch basins. • Park maintenance, fallen public trees and unsafe municipal

municipal bins. • Potholes, damaged street signs, municipal streetlights and blocked catch basins. • Park maintenance, fallen public trees and unsafe municipal pathways. • Request intake, classification, response targets, status tracking and escalation. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-SRM-01 | TRAINING ONLY SERVICE REQUEST MANAGEMENT SRM 1 | How to submit a service request Contact routes, intake fields and what happens next 1.1 Accepted channels Channel Availability / what to expect Cedarhaven Service Portal Available for electronic submissions at any time; automated reference number after successful submission. 311 contact centre Staffed Monday-Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., excluding Town-observed holidays. Town Hall front desk Staff can help record requests during the same business hours; no separate priority. Accessible intake Residents may request telephone assistance or alternate-format confirmation via 311 during staffed hours. The guide deliberately does not provide a public website URL, street address, email address or telephone number other than the generic 311 service name. Do not invent one. 1.2 Intake information • Required: issue category, location or nearest intersection, clear description, and date first

eric 311 service name. Do not invent one. 1.2 Intake information • Required: issue category, location or nearest intersection, clear description, and date first noticed (if known). • Useful but optional: photo, hazard description, reference landmark, and a contact method for updates. • For a missed collection, the collection date, material type, set-out time and bin condition are additionally needed (see page 4). • Requests involving private property may require landowner consent before municipal staff can enter. 1.3 Eligibility and ownership The 311 team checks whether the issue concerns a Town-owned asset or Town-managed service. It may forward eligible by-law complaints to Enforcement and permit questions to Development Services. Routing is not a promise that an investigation or approval will occur. Safety first. For immediate danger to life, fire, suspected gas leaks or a serious active medical emergency, contact emergency services. Do not treat a 311 submission as an emergency

diate danger to life, fire, suspected gas leaks or a serious active medical emergency, contact emergency services. Do not treat a 311 submission as an emergency response. For an immediate water-main break, contact 311 during staffed hours; outside those hours the guide does not provide an after-hours phone number. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-SRM-01 | TRAINING ONLY SERVICE REQUEST MANAGEMENT SRM 2 | Priority and response standards Targets describe first response, not guaranteed completion 2.1 Service priority matrix Priority Example / trigger Initial action target P1 - urgent Open sinkhole, downed electrical wire, exposed sharp debris on a busy public path. Staff assessment within 4 staffed hours; make-safe action targeted within 1 business day when feasible. P2 - high Damaged stop sign, severe drainage blocking an arterial road, large fallen limb obstructing a sidewalk. Assessment within 1 business day; work scheduling after assessment. P3 - standard Routine pothole, flickering streetlight, ordinary park litter. Assessment within 3 business days; work according to service-specific targets. P4 - information General question, follow-up or request that needs another department. Acknowledgement within 2 business days; referral if appropriate. 2.2 How time is measured • Business day:

n, follow-up or request that needs another department. Acknowledgement within 2 business days; referral if appropriate. 2.2 How time is measured • Business day: Monday-Friday excluding Town-observed holidays. • Staffed hour: time within the 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. weekday contact-centre schedule. • An online request filed outside staffed hours enters the triage queue at the next staffed opening. • Targets can change following field assessment, severe weather, contractor availability or access restrictions. 2.3 Distinguish the milestones Acknowledgement confirms receipt and issues a case identifier. Assessment identifies severity, jurisdiction and next action. Make-safe addresses an immediate hazard. Resolution records the final outcome. These are not interchangeable. Important exception. A fallen overhead utility wire is treated as an immediate hazard; residents must keep clear and contact emergency services or the utility provider. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-SRM-01 | TRAINING ONLY SERVICE REQUEST MANAGEMENT SRM 3 | Curbside waste and missed collection Eligibility criteria, evidence, collection attempt and exceptions 3.1 When to report a missed pickup A missed garbage, recycling or organics pickup may be reported after 7:00 p.m. on the scheduled collection day and within two business days after that day. Early reports are recorded as inquiries, not confirmed missed-collection service requests. 3.2 What residents must provide • Full service address, material stream (garbage, recycling or organics), scheduled collection date and time the bin was set out. • Whether the bin was visible and accessible at the curb by 7:00 a.m. on collection day. • Whether a rejection tag was attached, the lid was closed, and any vehicle or snowbank blocked access. • A photo is helpful but not mandatory; personal contact information is optional unless an update is requested. 3.3 Eligibility and attempt window Situation

ss. • A photo is helpful but not mandatory; personal contact information is optional unless an update is requested. 3.3 Eligibility and attempt window Situation Town response On-time, compliant set-out; no obstruction Accept missed-collection case and target a return pickup within 2 business days after validation. Bin placed out after 7:00 a.m. Not eligible for a missed-pickup return; advise next scheduled day. Rejection tag for contamination / oversized contents Not eligible until corrected; advise resident to follow collection rules. Blocked by parked vehicle, snowbank or inaccessible gate May be declined; resident should remove the obstruction before next service. After a valid report, residents should leave the bin at the curb until 7:00 p.m. of the next business day, unless doing so creates a safety obstruction. A return pickup is a target, not a guarantee. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-SRM-01 | TRAINING ONLY SERVICE REQUEST MANAGEMENT SRM 4 | Roads, streetlights, drainage and water Category-specific routing and field service standards 4.1 Potholes and roadway surfaces For routine potholes on Town-maintained roads (P3), Roads Operations targets an assessment within 3 business days and a repair within 15 business days after assessment, subject to weather and materials. Report the nearest address or intersection, travel direction, lane and hazard size if safe. A road collapse, sinkhole or hazard causing immediate danger is P1; see page 3. Provincial highways, private roads and roads outside Cedarhaven are referred to their owners and are not scheduled as Town repairs. 4.2 Streetlights and traffic signs Issue Target or rule Flickering or unlit Town streetlight P3 assessment within 3 business days; repair target 10 business days after assessment if Town-owned. Damaged stop sign P2 initial assessment within 1 business day;

assessment within 3 business days; repair target 10 business days after assessment if Town-owned. Damaged stop sign P2 initial assessment within 1 business day; make-safe / temporary control according to field risk. Traffic-signal outage Urgent safety referral to Roads Operations; if traffic is dangerous contact emergency services. Private driveway or private parking-lot light Outside the Town streetlight program; contact property owner. 4.3 Flooding and blocked catch basins A blocked catch basin with standing water but no immediate roadway danger is normally P2 if a road is affected, otherwise P3. Flooding entering occupied buildings or undermining a roadway requires urgent safety escalation; do not promise a drainage response time beyond the priority assessment target. 4.4 Suspected water-main break Provide the location, visible leak description and any hazard. 311 records a referral to Water Operations. Water shutoff time, repair completion time and compensation eligibility are not

ble leak description and any hazard. 311 records a referral to Water Operations. Water shutoff time, repair completion time and compensation eligibility are not defined in this guide. Residents should avoid affected areas and follow any official safety direction. FICTIONAL POLICY • NOT FOR REAL MUNICIPAL OR LEGAL USE CH-SRM-01 | PAGE 5 OF 8

Broken play-equipment component Classify P1 if imminent injury risk; otherwise P2; field team decides whether to close the feature. Unsafe debris or glass on busy public pathway P1 if acute injury risk, otherwise P2 or P3 after assessment. Graffiti on Town-owned park structure P3 assessment; cleaning target within 10 business days after assessment. 5.2 Public and private trees For a tree or large branch blocking a public sidewalk, record location, obstruction and visible hazard; usually P2. For a downed tree resting on a power line, keep clear and seek emergency/utility assistance. Routine public-tree pruning is P3, with field

e hazard; usually P2. For a downed tree resting on a power line, keep clear and seek emergency/utility assistance. Routine public-tree pruning is P3, with field scheduling dependent on season and arborist availability. A tree entirely on private property is generally the owner's responsibility. If it violates a property-maintenance standard or creates an apparent nuisance, the resident may submit a by-law complaint under CH-BYL-02; municipal crews do not automatically cut private trees. 5.3 Sidewalk and winter-maintenance reports • Broken municipal sidewalk slab: routine P3 unless an acute trip hazard raises the priority. • Snow or ice on a Town sidewalk: assess according to weather event and pedestrian safety; normal time-to-clear is not published here. • Snow or ice on a private frontage: may be a by-law matter under CH-BYL-02; the Town does not guarantee private-property clearing via 311. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-SRM-01 | TRAINING ONLY SERVICE REQUEST MANAGEMENT SRM 6 | Request lifecycle and resident updates A trackable case is not the same as an approved action 6.1 Standard status definitions Status Meaning / action Submitted Request received and assigned a reference number; completeness not yet checked. Under Review Staff checks scope, location, evidence, duplication and priority. Assigned Responsible Town work group or partner has accepted the item for assessment or action. Scheduled Work visit or next action planned; no fixed appointment implied. In Progress Field or desk team has started the task or investigation. Completed Town has recorded its action or final decision; may include referral or no-work-required outcome. Closed - Not Eligible Outside jurisdiction, duplicate, insufficient information or ineligible service. 6.2 How updates work • The Service Portal shows the current status and most recent status note for users with a valid case

nt information or ineligible service. 6.2 How updates work • The Service Portal shows the current status and most recent status note for users with a valid case reference. • If the resident supplied an email and opted into updates, a notification is sent when the case is Assigned, Scheduled or Completed. • If the resident did not provide contact details, the case can still be processed, but proactive personal notifications are unavailable. • Sensitive enforcement information may be withheld from the resident-facing case notes. 6.3 Reopening A resident may request review of a completed service request within five business days after its completion if the reported condition persists. Reopening is discretionary after staff verification; after five business days, a new case should generally be filed. By-law investigations have separate disclosure and appeal procedures (CH-BYL-02). Dates matter. A Scheduled status is not a guaranteed visit date. The published performance targets concern

eparate disclosure and appeal procedures (CH-BYL-02). Dates matter. A Scheduled status is not a guaranteed visit date. The published performance targets concern categories and initial actions; never invent an individual crew appointment or a specific arrival time. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-SRM-01 | TRAINING ONLY SERVICE REQUEST MANAGEMENT SRM 7 | Duplicates, escalation and cross-service routing Protect resident privacy and avoid the wrong workflow 7.1 Duplicate prevention Requests may be considered duplicates if they concern the same location, issue category and observed condition within 72 hours, subject to staff review. A resident may be linked to the existing case rather than given an independent repair schedule. Materially worsening hazards are re-triaged even when an earlier case exists. 7.2 Escalation rules • If a P3 request has not been assessed after 3 business days, residents may ask 311 for a status review. • If a category-specific completion target has passed, 311 may send a follow-up to the owning work group; this does not guarantee immediate completion. • If a hazard becomes urgent, residents should report the changed conditions instead of relying on the previous priority. • For a submitted permit or business-licence

hazard becomes urgent, residents should report the changed conditions instead of relying on the previous priority. • For a submitted permit or business-licence application, contact Development Services through the process described in CH-PER-03. 7.3 Which process owns the issue? Resident situation Correct route Noise from a nearby renovation By-law complaint (CH-BYL-02), unless immediate danger. Need approval to build a new deck Permit application (CH-PER-03), not a service request. Contractor blocks the public sidewalk with materials 311 obstruction report; Development Services may also review encroachment permit compliance. Construction appears to violate approved permit Development Services compliance review; 311 can route the concern. Missed waste pickup 311 waste service request if eligible under page 4. 7.4 Privacy and records Only collect information reasonably needed to process the case. Internal case notes and third-party identities are not available through this public guide. Not covered. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-BYL-02 | TRAINING ONLY BY-LAW ENFORCEMENT Purpose, coverage & document map CH-BYL-02 | Version 1.0 | Effective 01 Sep 2026 Important. Cedarhaven is a fictional Ontario town and the following rules are invented for an AI retrieval/coding assessment. They are not enforceable legislation or advice about real municipalities. References to deadlines, officer powers and penalties apply only within this exercise. Why this guide exists. Residents need to know what conduct is covered by the Town's simulated by-laws, when to file a complaint, and what the investigation process can and cannot promise. A 311 complaint is a request for review, not an automatic penalty. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-BYL-02 | TRAINING ONLY BY-LAW ENFORCEMENT BYL 1 | Noise and construction activity Allowed hours, exemptions and complaint examples 1.1 Residential amplified sound Amplified music, outdoor speakers and similar amplified sound must not create unreasonable disturbance in residential areas during 10:00 p.m.-7:00 a.m. on all days. During other hours, persistent excessive noise may still be reviewed if the facts support a nuisance concern; the hours are not a blanket permission to disturb neighbours. 1.2 Construction equipment hours Day Permitted routine construction-noise hours Monday-Friday 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. Saturday 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. Sunday or Town-observed holiday No routine construction noise permitted Noise from powered saws, excavation equipment, jackhammers and similar construction equipment follows this schedule. The rule applies to private contractors as well as homeowners. A building permit does not extend permissible noise hours. 1.3

n equipment follows this schedule. The rule applies to private contractors as well as homeowners. A building permit does not extend permissible noise hours. 1.3 Narrow exemptions • Immediate emergency repair: work needed to prevent imminent danger or restore an essential utility may occur outside the routine construction window. • Town-authorized emergency operations: municipal emergency crews may operate when needed for public safety. • Special noise exemption: Development Services may issue a specific written exemption for identified dates/times; this guide does not provide its fee or application turnaround. An ordinary building permit is not such an exemption. 1.4 Examples A homeowner using a power saw at 8:00 a.m. Saturday is outside the permitted window. The same activity at 10:00 a.m. Saturday is within the routine construction-noise window, although other by-law standards may still apply. An emergency utility repair at 2:00 a.m. can qualify only if the facts meet the emergency

ruction-noise window, although other by-law standards may still apply. An emergency utility repair at 2:00 a.m. can qualify only if the facts meet the emergency exception. Document gap. The guide does not define an objective decibel limit, measurement method, fine amount or automatic exemption for weddings or community festivals. Do not invent any of these. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-BYL-02 | TRAINING ONLY BY-LAW ENFORCEMENT BYL 2 | Property standards and outdoor maintenance Grass, waste accumulation, vacant properties and notices 2.1 Grass and vegetation From May 1 to September 30, maintained portions of residential front and side yards must not have unmanaged grass or weeds exceeding 20 cm in height. Deliberately maintained naturalized gardens are not automatically a violation; Enforcement evaluates maintenance, sightlines and nuisance conditions. 2.2 Outdoor accumulation • Garbage, loose food waste or household debris must not accumulate outdoors in a way that attracts pests or creates a health nuisance. • Construction materials may be stored temporarily on the private worksite if reasonably organized and safe; material on a public sidewalk requires separate encroachment approval (CH-PER-03). • A resident should not enter a neighbour's yard to photograph a suspected violation. roachment approval (CH-PER-03). • A resident should not enter a neighbour's yard to photograph a suspected violation. Photos taken legally from public areas may be submitted. 2.3 Typical enforcement sequence Step Standard practice Observe / verify Officer assesses the location and available evidence before finding a breach. Written compliance notice For ordinary vegetation or storage violations, the notice generally gives 7 calendar days to correct. Reinspection Officer checks after the stated period; more action may follow if the breach remains. Immediate hazard exception If there is an urgent public safety hazard, the Town may act or refer urgently without waiting 7 days. 2.4 Complaints involving vacant lots Vacant private lots are subject to the outdoor storage and hazard provisions. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-BYL-02 | TRAINING ONLY BY-LAW ENFORCEMENT BYL 3 | On-street parking Time limits, overnight restriction and jurisdiction 3.1 General daytime parking limit On local residential streets without a more restrictive posted sign, the maximum continuous parking period is 3 hours between 9:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.. Moving a car a few metres on the same block solely to reset the limit does not create a fresh allowance for this exercise. 3.2 Seasonal overnight restriction November 15-April 15 inclusive, parking on Town streets is prohibited from 2:00 a.m. to 6:00 a.m. to support winter operations, unless a valid Town-issued exemption expressly applies. The guide does not specify how to apply for an overnight exemption. 3.3 Signs and emergency restrictions Condition How to interpret it Posted no-parking / no-stopping sign Follow the sign even if it is stricter than the default 3-hour rule. Signed accessible parking space Use only with proper authorization;

Temporary snow-event restriction Obey current official notices and posted temporary restrictions. Private shopping-centre parking lot Generally managed by the private owner, not this on-street provision. 3.4 Reporting a concern Report location, vehicle description, time observed, relevant signs and whether access is blocked. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-BYL-02 | TRAINING ONLY BY-LAW ENFORCEMENT BYL 4 | Fences, lots and pool-related barriers Height rules are separate from building-permit rules 4.1 Maximum heights for ordinary residential fences Location Maximum height Front yard (between front property line and building front wall) 1.2 metres Side yard behind the front wall 1.8 metres Rear yard 1.8 metres Within a visibility triangle at a street corner 0.9 metres Fence heights are measured from the finished grade on the fence owner's side unless an officer determines another reference grade is required for uneven terrain. On corner lots, the 0.9 m visibility-triangle cap takes precedence where applicable. 4.2 Permits and variances An ordinary private residential fence generally does not require a building permit under CH-PER-03. That does not waive the height limits here. A resident seeking a taller fence must seek a written variance review before construction; approval is not guaranteed and

does not waive the height limits here. A resident seeking a taller fence must seek a written variance review before construction; approval is not guaranteed and the variance fee is not stated in these documents. 4.3 Pool barriers A barrier around a newly installed private outdoor pool requires a separate pool-barrier permit from Development Services before installation. Pool-specific barrier design, gate-latch measurements and permit fee are deliberately outside this guide; do not claim a general 1.8 m fence automatically satisfies the pool standard. 4.4 Boundary disagreements The Town can assess compliance with the simulated fence-height rule, but it does not settle property-line ownership disputes. A private survey or professional advice may be needed. Neither the precise survey process nor cost is provided. Cross-document rule. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-BYL-02 | TRAINING ONLY BY-LAW ENFORCEMENT BYL 6 | Complaints, inspection and outcome An allegation is not a determination of non-compliance 6.1 Filing and basic evidence Submit a non-emergency complaint through 311 or the Cedarhaven Service Portal as described in CH-SRM-01. Include the location, type of concern, approximate dates/times, what was observed and any legally obtained supporting photos. Anonymous complaints may be accepted but can be harder to verify. 6.2 Intake and investigation workflow Stage Meaning Submitted Complaint logged; complainant receives a case reference if available. Triage Enforcement checks jurisdiction, urgency, duplicates and sufficiency of details. Investigation Officer may review records, inspect from lawful vantage points, or seek further evidence. Notice / education If verified, officer may issue guidance or a written compliance notice. Reinspection / action Officer verifies correction and decides whether a

tice / education If verified, officer may issue guidance or a written compliance notice. Reinspection / action Officer verifies correction and decides whether a further enforcement measure is appropriate. Closed Case concluded, including no violation found, lack of evidence or successful compliance. 6.3 Timelines and limits • Non-urgent complaints target triage within 3 business days. This is not a promise of inspection or resolution within three days. • Urgent public safety concerns are referred for immediate risk-based response; contact emergency services when life safety is at issue. • For common property-standard notices, the typical correction window is 7 calendar days after service (see page 3). • Investigation duration depends on evidence, property access, repeat visits and legal process. No universal completion deadline is stated. 6.4 Disclosure to complainant Residents may receive limited status information such as "under review" or "closed". Officer notes, personal details of

is stated. 6.4 Disclosure to complainant Residents may receive limited status information such as "under review" or "closed". Officer notes, personal details of alleged offenders, witness identities and penalty records are not automatically released through 311 or the chatbot. No guaranteed outcome. A report does not automatically cause a citation, ticket, licence suspension, removal of a structure or entry onto private property. A business licence does not approve an outdoor patio in the public right-of-way. A general

ng permit does not authorize construction noise outside normal hours. A business licence does not approve an outdoor patio in the public right-of-way. A general fence exemption from building permits does not override the fence by-law. Individual approvals are limited to their written scope. 7.3 Facts that cannot be inferred from this corpus • Specific fines for noise, parking or tall fences. • An officer's name, a personal phone number or the identity of a complainant. • Actual by-law complaint history or whether a named property has been charged. • Exact decibel thresholds, detailed swimming-pool barrier specifications or property-line survey costs. • A guaranteed investigation completion date or an automatic right to compensation. CEDARHAVEN / MUNICIPAL SERVICE LIBRARY CH-PER-03 | TRAINING ONLY PERMITS AND LICENSING PER 1 | Sheds and accessory structures Thresholds are specific to this exercise and not real law 1.1 Small detached storage-shed exemption A detached storage shed accessory to a single detached dwelling is exempt from a Cedarhaven building permit only when all of these conditions are satisfied: • Floor area is 12.0 square metres or less (exactly 12.0 m2 qualifies). • Total structure height is 3.0 metres or less. • No plumbing or electrical service is installed. • It is not used for sleeping, commercial occupancy or another habitable use. • It is entirely outside registered utility easements and does not conflict with a required setback. If any condition fails, a building-permit review is required. Example: a 14 m2 storage shed requires a building permit even if it is only 2.5 m high.
